summaryPoints: Bangladesh recovered from early pressure in the first innings, anchored by Mominul Haque's resolute 176 to post 513.
Sri Lanka replied strongly with 713/9, powered by BKG Mendis's commanding century (196) to swing the contest.
Bangladesh added 307/5 in their second innings led by Mominul Haque's masterclass (105) to seize control.
A resilient final-day rearguard ensured the match concluded in a fiercely contested draw.

The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 176 from Mominul Haque, complemented by a commanding 236-run stand between Mushfiqur Rahim and Mominul Haque that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.91 RPO. Sri Lanka's bowling response was spearheaded by HMRKB Herath (4/150), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Finishing at 513/10 (129.6 ov), Bangladesh established an overwhelming first-innings foundation that firmly dictated the terms of the match.

summaryTab.matchStory: Bangladesh recovered from early pressure in the first innings, anchored by Mominul Haque's resolute 176 to post 513. Sri Lanka replied strongly with 713/9, powered by BKG Mendis's commanding century (196) to swing the contest. Bangladesh added 307/5 in their second innings led by Mominul Haque's masterclass (105) to seize control. A resilient final-day rearguard ensured the match concluded in a fiercely contested draw.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Zahur Ahmed Chowdhury Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Bangladesh posted 513/10 (129.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Sri Lanka countered with 713/9 (199.3 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 308-Run Stand: Dhananjaya Silva & BKG Mendis, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Mominul Haque delivered a masterclass for Bangladesh (281 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Match Drawn 47%) and allowing Match Drawn to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Bangladesh faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Match Drawn's bowling unit, bolstered by BKG Mendis (196 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Match drawn in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Match Drawn's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Bangladesh produced fighting phases, Match Drawn won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
